title: THE LORD'S SHARE FROM THE SPOILS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Divide the spoils equally between the soldiers who took part in the battle and the rest of the community. From the soldiers who fought in the battle, set apart as tribute for the Lord one out of every five hundred, whether people, cattle, donkeys or sheep. Take this tribute from their half share and give it to Eleazar the priest as the Lord's part. - Num 31:27-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now comes the careful, orderly division of everything gained. The plunder was split between the soldiers who fought and the community who stayed behind — and a portion was set apart specifically as the Lord's part, given to the priests. Even in the aftermath of war, God taught His people to honour Him first with what they had received.

There are two quiet lessons here. First, God is fair. Those who fought and those who waited both shared in the outcome; He does not overlook anyone's part. In the kingdom of God, the one who works and the one who supports the work both share in the reward (John 4:36-38). Second, whatever we gain ultimately belongs to God, and honouring Him with the first and best of it keeps our hearts in the right place.

We do not give to God because He needs our goods — He owns everything already. We give because giving reminds us who the true Owner is, and it loosens the grip of greed on our hearts. Jesus taught that where our treasure is, our heart will follow (Matt 6:21). When we set apart a portion for the Lord, we are really setting our hearts on Him. And we give cheerfully, knowing that in Christ we have already received the greatest gift of all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you honour God first with what comes into your hands?
2. How does it encourage you that God rewards both frontline workers and quiet supporters?
3. What might God be asking you to hold more loosely?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Generous God, everything I have comes from You and belongs to You. Teach me to honour You first and to give with a cheerful, trusting heart. Amen.
